process_area.title: Store Visit, Field Coaching & Retail Standards Execution

value_stream.name: Field Retail Operations, Regional/District Management & Multi-Store Retail Execution Network

fields.Participants: Director Field Retail Operations, Store Managers (VS-07), Analytics (VS-28), Travel/Fleet (VS-06/VS-61)
fields.Trigger: Cadence policy; territory assignment (W5106); monthly/quarterly plan
fields.Volume: ~33 stores per Regional Manager / ~15 per District Manager (profile §12.1) × tier-based cadence (DM ~monthly; RM ~quarterly+) → ~180–360 visits/yr per DM, ~130–200 per RM

workflows.name: Regional/District Store-Visit Cadence, Routing & Itinerary Planning

Automation Opportunity: - Cadence calendar auto-generation by tier; route optimization; pre-visit brief auto-population
Controls: - CTL-762 (ensure controlled execution — Store Visit, Field Coaching & Retail Standards Execution (PA-177.2).)
- CTL-762: cadence per policy (tier-based); unannounced-visit ratio enforced; visit log complete
Cross-references: - links to VS-07 (store ops), VS-06/VS-61 (travel/fleet); W5106 (territory), W5109 (tiering), W5114 (audit), W5118 (action-items)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cadence-failure risk**: Manager can't fit visits into the month (documented pain — "Regional Managers with ~33 stores per RM (District Managers ~15) struggle to fit monthly reviews into a 20-working-day month"); mitigated by tier-based cadence + routing optimization
- **Predictability risk**: All visits announced → stores prepare/gaming; mitigated by unannounced-visit ratio
- **Travel-cost risk**: Inefficient routing → cost/time waste; mitigated by route optimization
System Touchpoints: - Field-visit calendar (new/VS-63 task system); store P&L (W5109); action-items (W5118); analytics (VS-28); travel/fleet (VS-06/VS-61)

steps.activity: Set the visit cadence: standard visit frequency by store tier (A/B/C/D from W5109), the visit-type mix (full audit, coaching, drop-in, targeted), and the calendar build across the territory
Optimize routing & logistics: route/travel plan (island geography), the unannounced-visit ratio for objectivity, and the pre-visit prep (performance review, prior action-items W5118)
Communicate & coordinate: share the cadence with Store Managers (the announced portion), coordinate with LP/operations-standards specialists, and log the plan in the field system

fields.Participants: Store Manager (VS-07), Department Supervisors, LP (VS-23), CX (VS-13), Facilities (VS-138)
fields.Volume: ~2,400–4,800 visits/yr chain-wide (200 stores × 12–24 tier-based visits/store/yr) across ~19 field managers (~6 RMs + ~13 DMs)

workflows.name: Store-Visit Execution, Retail-Standards Audit & Compliance Scoring

Automation Opportunity: - Mobile standards-audit app with auto-scoring; photo-evidence capture; auto-action-item creation
Controls: - CTL-762: structured checklist used; audit competency certified (W5108); independent assurance cross-check (VS-146)
Cross-references: - links to VS-07 (store ops), VS-24 (HSE), VS-23 (shrink), VS-146 (assurance); W5113 (cadence), W5115 (coaching), W5118 (action-items), W5120 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Shallow-audit risk**: Rushed visit → missed standards; mitigated by structured checklist + time allocation
- **Scoring-inconsistency risk**: Different managers score differently → unreliable benchmark; mitigated by certification (W5108) + W5120 consistency analytics
- **Gaming risk**: Store prepares for announced visits; mitigated by unannounced-visit ratio (W5113) + independent assurance (VS-146)
System Touchpoints: - Field-audit/standards app (new); store P&L (W5109); CX (VS-13); shrink (VS-23); HSE (VS-24); action-items (W5118); analytics (W5120)

steps.activity: Execute the store walk & standards audit: opening/closing, salesfloor, lumber yard, receiving/backroom, customer service, restrooms, safety/HSE (links VS-24), and the structured retail-standards checklist scoring
Review operating performance with the Store Manager: P&L (W5109), CX, shrink, staff, prior action-items (W5118), and the coaching conversation (W5115)
Document & log the visit: the standards score, findings, action-items assigned (W5118), and the system entry for analytics (W5120)

fields.Participants: Store Managers (VS-07), HR/HRBP (VS-103), L&D (VS-19.4), Director Field Retail Operations
fields.Trigger: Store visit (W5114); performance cycle; development plan
fields.Volume: ~15 store managers per District Manager; ~33 per Regional Manager (profile §12.1)

Automation Opportunity: - Coaching-conversation template/prompt; development-plan tracker; action-item auto-creation
Controls: - CTL-762 (ensure controlled execution — Store Visit, Field Coaching & Retail Standards Execution (PA-177.2).)
- CTL-762: structured coaching method used; coaching documented; formal-action cases HRBP-supported (VS-103/VS-84)
Cross-references: - links to VS-19.1 (performance), VS-103 (HR), VS-84 (labor relations), VS-19.4 (L&D); W5114 (visit), W5118 (action-items), W5120 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Avoidance risk**: Manager skips the hard conversation → underperformance persists; mitigated by structured method + HRBP support
- **Inconsistency risk**: Coaching quality varies by manager; mitigated by certification (W5108) + W5120 quality analytics
- **Documentation risk**: Un-documented coaching → no audit trail for formal action; mitigated by step-3 logging
System Touchpoints: - Performance/development (VS-19.1); HRBP/case (VS-103); action-items (W5118); L&D (VS-19.4); labor relations (VS-84)
Time Estimate: - ~30–60 min coaching per store manager per visit

steps.activity: Prepare the coaching: review the Store Manager's performance (W5109), strengths/gaps, the development plan, and prior coaching follow-ups
Conduct the coaching conversation: structured feedback (situation-behavior-impact), goal-setting, the development action, and the performance-conduct conversation where needed (links VS-84/VS-19.1)
Document & follow-up: log the coaching, the agreed actions (W5118), the development plan update, and escalate performance cases to HR where formal action is needed

fields.Participants: Store Ops (VS-07), Merchandising (VS-01/VS-55), Pricing (VS-01.2/VS-118), LP (VS-23), Planogram (VS-55), Labeling (VS-151)

Automation Opportunity: - Mobile planogram/price-audit app; shelf-photo vs planogram image-match; price-file auto-reconcile
Controls: - CTL-762: shelf price reconciled to price-file (VS-118); planogram compliance (VS-55); price-tag presence (RA 7394/VS-151)
Cross-references: - links to VS-55 (planogram), VS-118 (price integrity), VS-151 (labeling), VS-14 (promo); W5114 (visit), W5118 (action-items)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Price-integrity risk**: Shelf price ≠ system price → RA 7394 exposure + revenue leakage; mitigated by reconciliation + VS-118 escalation
- **Planogram-drift risk**: Non-compliant planogram → lost sales/space productivity; mitigated by audit + reset (VS-55)
- **Audit-fatigue risk**: Too many audits → shallow checks; mitigated by focused campaign-based audits
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 hrs per visit on retail-execution standards

steps.activity: Audit the retail-execution standards: planogram compliance (VS-55), price/shelf-label accuracy & price-tag presence (VS-151/RA 7394), promotional-signage compliance (VS-14), merchandising standards, and end-cap/display execution
Reconcile to source-of-truth: spot-check shelf price vs POS/price-file (VS-118 revenue assurance), planogram vs space plan (VS-55), and signage vs promo calendar (VS-14)
Log discrepancies & assign action: price-tag reprint (VS-151), planogram reset (VS-55), promo-correction (VS-14), the action-items (W5118), and the pricing-integrity escalation if systemic (VS-118)

fields.Participants: Competitive Intelligence (VS-57), Marketing (VS-14), Merchandising (VS-01), Strategy (VS-33), Store Managers (VS-07)
fields.Trigger: Store visit (W5114); competitive activity; market shift

Automation Opportunity: - Mobile intelligence-submission app; photo capture; de-duplication; insight-to-action workflow
Controls: - CTL-762 (ensure controlled execution — Store Visit, Field Coaching & Retail Standards Execution (PA-177.2).)
- CTL-762: intelligence structured & timestamped; de-duplicated; fed to VS-57 competitive-intelligence program
Cross-references: - links to VS-57 (competitive intelligence), VS-14 (marketing), VS-01 (merch), VS-33 (strategy); W5114 (visit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Anecdote risk**: Intelligence not structured → unusable; mitigated by structured submission
- **Duplication risk**: Same observation from multiple sources; mitigated by de-duplication
- **Inaction risk**: Intelligence collected but not acted on; mitigated by step-3 insight-to-action
System Touchpoints: - Competitive intelligence (VS-57); pricing response (VS-57.2/VS-01.2); marketing (VS-14); strategy (VS-33); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Collect field intelligence: competitor store activity (new openings, closures, format changes), local pricing/promo observations, assortment trends, and customer/market signals — feeding the competitor-visit program (links VS-57 W624/W1661/W1910)
Submit & consolidate: structured intelligence submission to the competitive-intelligence system (VS-57), de-duplicated and timestamped

steps.a: Director Field Retail Operations / Competitive Intel Lead
steps.activity: Feed insights to action: competitive response (VS-57.2 pricing), assortment (VS-01), marketing (VS-14), and strategy (VS-33)

fields.Participants: Store Managers (VS-07), functional leads (Merch/IT/HR/Facilities/LP), Director Field Retail Operations

workflows.name: Field Action-Item Tracking, Follow-Up & CAP Closure

Automation Opportunity: - Single action-item/CAP tracker; overdue auto-alert; effectiveness-verification workflow
Controls: - CTL-762: every finding has an assigned action-item; overdue escalated; effectiveness verified before closure
Cross-references: - links to VS-63 (task system), VS-133 (CI); W5114/W5115/W5116 (sources), W5122 (escalation), W5120 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Drop-through risk**: Action-items created but not closed → no improvement; mitigated by tracking + overdue chase
- **Closure-without-effectiveness risk**: Marked done but not effective → recurrence; mitigated by effectiveness verification
- **System-fragmentation risk**: Action-items in email/spreadsheets, not a system; mitigated by a single tracker
System Touchpoints: - Action-item/CAP tracker (links VS-63 task system); field dashboard (W5127); escalation (W5122); analytics (W5120); CI (VS-133)

steps.activity: Create & assign action-items: from each visit/audit/coaching, assign owner, due-date, priority, and the corrective-action plan (CAP)
Track & follow-up: monitor open items, chase overdue, re-visit verification, and escalate stalled items (W5122)
Close & verify effectiveness: verify the fix is effective (not just done), close the CAP, and feed lessons to analytics (W5120) & CI (VS-133)

fields.Participants: Regional/District Managers, Store Ops (VS-07), HR (VS-103), Strategy (VS-33), Marketing/Merch (VS-14/VS-01)
fields.Trigger: Cadence; new program launch; recognition cycle

workflows.name: Field Communication, Regional Meetings & Best-Practice Sharing

Automation Opportunity: - Best-practice library/knowledge hub; meeting-analytics; two-way feedback channel
Controls: - CTL-762 (ensure controlled execution — Store Visit, Field Coaching & Retail Standards Execution (PA-177.2).)
- CTL-762: cadence disciplined; best practices documented & shared; two-way feedback captured
Cross-references: - links to VS-63 (store comms), VS-30.3 (knowledge), VS-134 (OCM), VS-103 (HR); W5112 (recognition), W5120 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Information-silo risk**: Best practices stay in one region; mitigated by cross-regional forum + library
- **Overload risk**: Too many meetings → manager time away from stores; mitigated by disciplined cadence
- **One-way risk**: HQ cascades but doesn't listen → field disengagement; mitigated by two-way feedback
System Touchpoints: - Field comms (links VS-63); best-practice library (VS-30.3 knowledge); recognition (W5112); OCM (VS-134); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Run the regional meetings: weekly regional manager forum (performance, issues, HQ updates), and the monthly store-manager regional meeting
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Regional Managers

steps.activity: Share best practices & recognition: top-performer showcase (links W5112), the field best-practice library, and cross-store peer learning
Cascade HQ programs & gather field feedback: new-program communication (links VS-63/VS-134 OCM), two-way feedback to HQ, and the change-readiness input (VS-134)
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Strategy / OCM

fields.Participants: Analytics (VS-28), Store Ops (VS-07), Strategy (VS-33), HR (VS-103), LP (VS-23), CX (VS-13)

workflows.name: Field Coaching Quality, Visit Effectiveness & Standards-Compliance Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Field-effectiveness dashboard; gaming-detection analytics; outcome-linkage modeling
Controls: - CTL-762 (ensure controlled execution — Store Visit, Field Coaching & Retail Standards Execution (PA-177.2).)
- CTL-762: outcome (not just activity) measured; consistency checked vs assurance (VS-146); improvement actions tracked (VS-133)
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics), VS-146 (assurance), VS-133 (CI), VS-36 (governance); W5114 (standards), W5118 (action-items), W5127 (dashboard)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vanity-metric risk**: Measuring activity (visits done) not outcome (improvement); mitigated by effectiveness/outcome metrics
- **Gaming-blindness risk**: Failing to detect score inflation; mitigated by consistency analytics + assurance reconciliation
- **Inaction risk**: Analytics without improvement action; mitigated by step-3 review & CI (VS-133)
System Touchpoints: - Field dashboard (W5127); analytics (VS-28); standards scores (W5114); action-items (W5118); assurance (VS-146); CI (VS-133)

steps.activity: Measure coaching & visit effectiveness: visit cadence adherence, action-item closure rate/effectiveness, coaching-quality scores, and the visit-to-performance-improvement linkage
Measure standards-compliance consistency: audit-score consistency across managers (W5114), the gaming-detection signal, and the independent-assurance reconciliation (VS-146)
steps.r: Analytics / Director Field Retail Operations / LP

steps.activity: Review & improve: leadership review (VS-36), the field-program improvement actions (VS-133), and the recognition/feedback to field managers (W5112)
